blocks.text: Mr. Doclens is an 85-year-old man with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy and chronic systolic heart failure, admitted 09/17 with acute on chronic decompensated heart failure, his fourth heart failure hospitalization in six months. He was diuresed with IV furosemide with.limited response; diuresis was complicated by acute kidney injury on CKD stage 4 (creatinine 2.4 baseline, peak 3.1)..Guideline-directed medical therapy could not be up-titrated because of symptomatic hypotension (SBP 82-90) and renal function; sacubitril/valsartan and spironolactone were stopped.
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: On hospital day 2 he developed fever and a right lower lobe infiltrate. CT angiogram showed no evidence of pulmonary embolism and right lower lobe consolidation. He completed a course of ceftriaxone and azithromycin; the pneumonia resolved clinically and radiographically by 09/26.
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: Cardiology (Dr. Hamid Sousa) saw him 09/22: stage D heart failure, NYHA class IV symptoms: at rest, not a candidate for advanced therapies (LVAD or transplant). His ICD was deactivated on 09/28 per the patient's and family's wishes.
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: Palliative care was consulted 09/25. In a family meeting the patient, who has moderate Alzheimer's dementia with fluctuating capacity, and his daughter (health care power of attorney) chose comfort-focused care and hospice at home. Code status changed to DNR/DNI.
blocks.label: text

blocks.text: NYHA class IV symptoms at rest despite maximally tolerated therapy.
blocks.label: text
